variants.summary:
Read-only review of variant-wise selling price and buying price (cost) in product create and edit, D:/Projects/elysium-erp at integration-wave2 (6a56a34). Nothing touches the landing-page builder (the owner dropped it; ncom handles that).

(1) Selling price per variant at creation: it works, including size x colour combinations. The /catalog/new grid (new-product.tsx:526-624) draws one row per combination (variant-grid.ts:26-43). Each row has a Price input whose placeholder is the main price (555-579). Typed prices that differ from the main price are sent as variantPrices with every value id of the row (245-252). The server matches them by value-id set, whatever the axis order (variant-prices.ts:31-61). It inserts each SKU at its own price (catalog.service.ts:334-368, 751) and refuses a price for a combination the axes do not make (CATALOG_VARIANT_INVALID). Server e2e (catalog-stock-ux.e2e.test.ts:187-221) and the console stack spec (catalog-stock.stack.ts:160) cover it. No price is ignored, overwritten, unsent or lost. The friction: every combination is typed one by one (no by-size or by-colour fill), changed rows are not highlighted, the main price stays required, and the client lets 0 or negative prices through to a server refusal.

(2) Changing prices later: yes, per variant. "Edit prices" on the product page (product-detail.tsx:497-517, 678-703) sends PUT /v1/catalog/prices, which is all-or-nothing and keeps price history, with a fixed reason. There is no bulk tool (all XL +100, set all, percent), no category-wide reprice, and the CSV price import has no template and no export of current prices. Adding a size later has no price field: the server gives new SKUs the cheapest existing price, archived SKUs included (catalog.service.ts:414-423, 830-834), and they go on sale straight away.

(3) Buying price: per-variant cost can be entered only on the Stock in hand page and in the new-product form's "in hand" mode, both only while the opening-stock window is open. It can also be typed line by line on Supply > Entries, one SKU per line with no product grid. The product page's Receive dialog takes one cost for all variants (stock-actions.tsx:281-312). So does the new-product form's supplier mode (new-product.tsx:303-314, 361), the only mode left once the window closes. This is the norm for a live brand, although the server takes a cost per line (supply.schemas.ts:303-326). The product page shows no cost at all (product-detail.tsx:68-70), yet the stock rows it already loads carry wacPoisha for read:cost roles (inventory.repository.ts:451-452), and they go unused. There is no last-cost or margin view anywhere. A standard buying price per variant fits invariant 5 if it lives in the supply module behind read:cost (design in the findings).

(4) Compare-at price: there is no merchant-set regular price. The website's compare-at comes only from flash sales. The product page and product cards never apply live flash prices, and the "on sale" filter returns nothing, while the cart does charge the flash price. So the shop shows one price and the cart another; the old site's product page showed the strike-through.

(5) Other friction: no barcode edit screen (the API exists), no photos per colour, no weight (couriers get the 500 g default), no "duplicate product", removing a size means archiving each variant one by one, adding a colour to a size-only product silently leaves the old variants on sale, AddVariants can write SKU code segments in a different order, the product spreadsheet import takes one price per product, and the size chart is only under the folded website section with no category default.

findings.what: Adding a size or colour later gives the new variants no price you can choose: they start at the CHEAPEST existing SKU's price, archived SKUs included, and are sellable at once. An XXL added to a shirt whose XXL should be ৳1,590 goes live at ৳1,490, or at an archived clearance price.
findings.evidence: AddVariants sends only `axes` (product-detail.tsx:814-817). The console's addVariants() accepts `pricePoisha` (api.ts:347), but the UI never passes it. extendMatrix falls back to `cheapest(existing)` (catalog.service.ts:417). `existing` comes from skusOfProduct, which has no status filter (catalog.repository.ts:503-506). New SKUs are inserted 'active'.
findings.proposal: (a) Server: extend `extendMatrixSchema` (catalog.schemas.ts:198-202) with `variantPrices` like createProduct's, and apply domain `variantPrices()` to `plan.additions` only. Exclude archived SKUs from `cheapest`, or better, default each new combination to an active sibling's price for the same size (XXL/Blue takes XXL/Red's price), and only then to the cheapest active price. (b) Console: before submitting, list the planned new rows with an editable price per row (placeholder = the default the server will use) and send them.

findings.what: The product page's Receive stock dialog takes ONE cost per piece for every variant, from a supplier and in hand alike. Variant-wise buying price (XL costs more than M) cannot be entered where stock is usually received.
findings.evidence: `costPoisha = positiveCost(takaToPoisha(costTaka))` (283) is applied to every line: `unitCostPoisha: costPoisha ?? '0'` (300, 312). QtyTable has only a Qty column (105-185). The server accepts a cost per line: createSupplySchema lines `{skuId, qty, unitCostPoisha}` (supply.schemas.ts:303-326), and pricedLines for stock in hand (stock-in-hand.schemas.ts:42-46).
findings.proposal: When `ability.can('read','Cost')`, add a 'Cost per piece' column to the receive QtyTable. Keep the common cost field as the fallback, using the `costOf(row)` pattern already in new-product.tsx:185-188 and stock-in-hand.tsx:441-443. Prefill each row from the standard buying price or the last received cost (see the supply design finding). Show Σ qty × cost per line as the total. Roles without read:cost still save a quantity-only draft (D-005).

findings.what: In the new-product form, cost per variant exists only in 'Already in hand' mode, and that mode exists only while the opening-stock window is open. 'Received from a supplier' mode hides the per-variant cost column and posts one cost for all variants. Per-variant costs typed in in-hand mode are thrown away when the person switches to supplier mode. Once Elysium closes its window, variant-wise buying price at creation is impossible.
findings.evidence: `showCostColumn = mayReceive && mayPrice && stockMode === 'in-hand'` (361). The supplier branch uses `unitCostPoisha: costPoisha ?? '0'` for every line (309-313), while the in-hand branch uses `costOf(line.row)` (292). `stockMode` is forced to 'supplier' when the window is closed (168). D-421 records 'one cost per piece' as an ASSUMED default.
findings.proposal: Show the per-variant cost column in both modes and use `costOf(row)` for supplier lines too: one-line change at 312 plus `costMissing` and `stockValue` at 208-222. Amend D-421 with a decision row. Add a stack-spec case that receives two variants at different costs, then checks sku_costs.wac_poisha for each.

findings.what: The product page shows a read:cost role no buying price at all: no average cost (WAC), no last cost, no margin per variant. The WAC per variant is already in the data the page loads and is discarded.
findings.evidence: The page comment says 'There is no cost on this page' (68-70). Its `listStock({ productId })` query (116-120) returns StockRow, which includes `wacPoisha` / `stockValuePoisha` for cost roles (stock list SQL selects `coalesce(c.wac_poisha,0)`, inventory.repository.ts:451-452; serializeFor strips them for others). VariantGrid never reads them (593-623). stock-levels.tsx:215-235 already renders the same field behind `mayReadCost`, so the pattern exists.
findings.proposal: Behind `ability.can('read','Cost')` and only when the field is present (as stock-levels.tsx does), add VariantGrid columns 'Avg cost' (WAC), 'Last cost' and 'Margin' = (price − WAC)/price, computed in the browser with bigint (basis points, no floats). Add a 'Stock value' tile (Σ stockValuePoisha). Show '—' when the SKU has no stock row or on_hand = 0 with WAC 0, because coalesce(…,0) otherwise reads as 'cost ৳0'. No catalog change; cost still leaves only through inventory/supply routes and serializeFor. Rewrite the page's doc comment.

findings.what: There is nowhere to keep a 'standard buying price' per variant (and per supplier) that pre-fills future receipts, and no 'last purchase cost' per SKU anywhere: supply_lines.unit_cost_poisha exists but no route reads it per SKU.
findings.evidence: Supply routes (supply.controller.ts:98-278) have no per-SKU cost read. Supply > Entries lines start blank (entries.tsx:85-88), and draft pricing starts blank (entries.tsx:606). The catalog schema forbids any cost column by design (packages/db/src/schema/catalog/index.ts:26-41).
findings.proposal: Design, compatible with invariant 5: table `supply.sku_purchase_prices` (id, org_id NOT NULL FK+index, sku_id, supplier_id NULL = any supplier, `standard_unit_cost_poisha bigint NOT NULL CHECK >= 0 AND <= 9e15`, updated_by, timestamps), unique (org_id, sku_id, coalesce(supplier_id, zero-uuid)). It gets RLS ENABLE+FORCE, composite FKs (org_id, sku_id)→catalog.skus and (org_id, supplier_id)→supply.suppliers (D-047), and the minimum erp_app grants. Add both spellings `standardUnitCostPoisha`/`standard_unit_cost_poisha` and `lastUnitCostPoisha`/`last_unit_cost_poisha` to COST_FIELDS; cost-fields.test.ts fails otherwise. Routes: `GET /v1/supply/sku-costs?productId=|skuIds=` (@RequireAbility read Cost) returns per SKU {standardUnitCostPoisha, lastUnitCostPoisha, lastReceivedOn, lastSupplierName}; the last cost is the newest received supply_lines row for that SKU, with stock-in-hand lines as fallback through InventoryApi, and product/SKU names come through CatalogApi (invariant 12). `PUT /v1/supply/sku-costs` (read Cost + create Supply, ≤500 lines, audited by the interceptor) sets standard prices, including by-size fill from the product page. The table is used only to PRE-FILL the receive dialog, Supply entries, draft pricing and the new-product cost column, with an optional 'remember these costs' tick on a receipt. It never feeds WAC or a journal: the actual cost still enters only through a posted receipt (invariant 2 and 5 unchanged). Never join it into catalog responses or the reseller allow-list. Tests: route-matrix fixtures and the cost sweep for the new routes, plus an integration test that a role without read:cost gets 403 and no field.

findings.what: Changing prices later is per-variant typing only: no 'all XL +৳100', 'set all to ৳1,490', '+10% on this category' or 'all Red −৳50'. A 5-size × 6-colour product needs 30 edits for one size-wide change, and catalog-wide reprices need a hand-built CSV.
findings.evidence: Edit mode turns each SKU's price cell into its own input (684-698). `changed` is built from those inputs only (497-504). The only other path is the SKU-code CSV (import.tsx PriceImport). PUT /v1/catalog/prices takes ≤500 explicit {skuId, pricePoisha} (catalog.schemas.ts:207-213).
findings.proposal: In Edit prices mode add a rule bar: [All | Size ▾ | Colour ▾] [Set to | + | − | %] [amount] [round to ৳10 ▾] Apply. It fills the inputs; nothing is saved until 'Save prices', which keeps one PUT with history. Put the arithmetic in a pure, property-tested `applyPriceRule(skus, rule)` in packages/domain/src/catalog (invariant 11), with rounding only through packages/domain/src/money (invariant 1), and refuse results ≤0. Add a catalog-wide version on the Products list (select products or a category → rule → dry-run preview like the price importer → commit through setPrices, in 500-SKU chunks or a new server endpoint in one transaction). Let the person type the price-history reason, e.g. 'Eid price', instead of the fixed 'Edited on the product page' (product-detail.tsx:511).

findings.what: Per-variant selling price at creation works but is laborious and easy to miss for a fashion brand. Every combination is typed separately (no 'price by size' that fills all colours), a row priced differently from the main price looks just like one using the placeholder, and the main 'Selling price' is required even when every variant has its own price.
findings.evidence: One input per row (564-577), placeholder = main price (568). `ready` requires `pricePoisha !== null` (224-225). The help text 'Leave a price blank to use the selling price' (stock-tools.en.ts:107-108) is the only hint.
findings.proposal: Above the grid, add a 'Price by size' strip (one input per chosen size) and a 'Price by colour' strip. Precedence: cell > size > colour > main price, resolved in a pure domain helper, with each cell's placeholder showing the price that will apply. Highlight rows whose price differs from the main price (semantic token, plus a 'own price' label beside the colour, per the a11y rules). Add a 'Fill column' button for cost and price. Default the main price to the lowest variant price when it is left blank, or rename it 'Default price'.

findings.what: The website's product page and product cards ignore live flash sales, and the 'On sale' filter returns nothing. The cart does charge the flash price, so a shopper sees ৳1,490 with no strike-through on the product page and ৳1,190 in the cart. The old site's product page showed the strike-through.
findings.evidence: `storefrontPrice({ id: sku.id, pricePoisha })` is called with no offers (storefront-public.service.ts:203), so compareAt is always null (price.ts:33-35). Cards hard-code `compareAt: null, onSale: false` (491-492, 535). `if (filter.onSale) conditions.push(sql`false`)` (catalog-web.repository.ts:234). The cart passes `flashPrices` to quoteCart (buying.service.ts:236-239; cart.ts:170-178). D-511 said 'M35 fills both'. Old site: `git show main:app/(store)/shop/[slug]/ProductDetailClient.js` line 226 renders flash.regularPrice line-through.
findings.proposal: Inject PROMO_API into the storefront public service the way flash-sales.reader.ts:26 does. Load live flash prices for the SKUs on the page and pass them to storefrontPrice (product page) and to the card min/max (cards: price = min effective price, compareAt = shelf price when lower, onSale = any SKU discounted). Implement the onSale filter as 'has an active SKU in a live flash sale' through a PromoApi id list. Add a stack test that the product page price equals the cart's unitPrice during a live sale.

findings.what: A variant has no compare-at ('regular' / MRP) price, so a brand cannot show a permanent '৳1,890 → ৳1,490' outside a flash sale, which modern shops do. The old site had none on products either.
findings.evidence: catalog.skus has only `price_poisha` (396). StorefrontPrice.compareAtPoisha is set only by a flash offer (price.ts:23-36).
findings.proposal: Add a nullable `compare_at_poisha bigint` on catalog.skus with CHECK (compare_at_poisha IS NULL OR compare_at_poisha > price_poisha). It is a selling-side field, not cost, and its name does not match the cost-column regex in cost-fields.test.ts. Record it in price history (extend the 0026 trigger or add a column). Edit it in the new-product grid and the Edit prices mode (optional 'Regular price' column with the same by-size fill), and in the price CSV (`compare_at_taka`). storefrontPrice: compareAt = flash ? max(shelf, compare_at) : compare_at. Keep it off the reseller allow-list. Note for the owner: a 'was' price must be a real recent price (consumer-protection risk), so consider warning when compare_at was never the actual price in the history.

findings.what: AddVariants sends axes in the attribute-list order (position, then code), while the new-product form sends size before colour. The server takes the request order as the SKU-code segment order, so variants added later can get `…-0007-RED-XL` while the originals are `…-0007-XL-RED`. That is inconsistent printed codes, and confusing for scanning and search.
findings.evidence: New product: `.sort((a,b) => rank(a.kind) - rank(b.kind) || a.position - b.position)` (171-173). AddVariants: `(attributes.data?.items ?? []).filter(...)` with no sort (807-809). The server uses `position: index` and comments that the request order is the code order (catalog.service.ts:680-686). listAttributes orders `by position, code` (repository 296), and with equal positions 'COLOUR' sorts before 'SIZE'. The Setup screen sets position = creation order (structure.tsx:437).
findings.proposal: Make the server own the order. In extendMatrix, take the axis order from the product's existing SKUs (the attribute order of the first SKU's values / its code), and for createProduct use kind rank then position. Or, as a minimum, apply new-product's `rank()` sort in AddVariants. Add an e2e test that adds XXL to a size × colour product whose Colour list sits before Size and checks the segment order.

findings.what: Choosing a value on an axis the product does not have yet (adding a colour to a size-only product) creates the full new matrix (M/Red, M/Blue…) and leaves every old size-only SKU (M, L…) active and on sale. The server reports them as `orphaned`; the UI drops that and shows only 'N variants added'.
findings.evidence: matrixPlan returns `orphaned` for existing keys not in the new axes, and extendMatrix returns them ('Reported, never removed', 444-445). AddVariants' onSuccess reads only `data.created.length` (819-823).
findings.proposal: Before submitting, show the plan from a dry-run flag or a client-side variantRows diff: 'Will add 6, and these 3 existing variants won't match: M, L, XL. Archive them? (their stock stays and can be transferred to the new variants)'. Archive on confirmation. After success, list `orphaned` with an Archive button. A stock-move helper (transfer M → M/Red) would be an inventory adjustment pair, so keep it out of scope or route it through approvals.

findings.what: Removing a size (stop selling XS in all 6 colours) means archiving 6 variants one by one, each with its own confirm dialog. In 'Add sizes or colours' an existing value cannot be unticked.
findings.evidence: A per-row Archive button opens a ConfirmDialog for one SKU (737-743, 771-773). The onToggle guard `if (list.includes(valueId) && existing(axis).includes(valueId)) return;` (844). PATCH /v1/catalog/skus/:id takes one SKU (catalog.controller.ts:268-275).
findings.proposal: Rename the section 'Sizes and colours' and let an existing value be unticked. Show 'Archive 6 variants of XS (stock 4 stays; can still be transferred/written off)' with one confirm. Add `PATCH /v1/catalog/skus` {skuIds[] ≤500, status} in one transaction (update Catalog, audited), with a route-matrix fixture. Re-ticking restores them.

findings.what: Supply > Entries is the one screen with a cost per line after go-live, but each line is one SKU chosen from a long dropdown, with no 'add product → all its sizes/colours' grid and no cost prefill. Receiving 30 variants of one style is 30 dropdown picks. Draft pricing likewise starts blank.
findings.evidence: blankLine() starts `unitCostTaka: ''` (87). Each row has a Select over `skuOptions` (445-459). Draft pricing uses `prices[line.skuId] ?? ''` (606). Stock in hand already has `addProduct` adding every active variant as a line (stock-in-hand.tsx:488-506).
findings.proposal: Reuse stock-in-hand's 'Add product' search in the Supply entry form: add every active variant as lines with Qty and Cost, a 'same cost for all' field, and by-size fill. Prefill cost from the standard or last cost (GET /v1/supply/sku-costs) for read:cost roles only. Do the same prefill in the draft-pricing table.

findings.what: Spreadsheet paths cannot carry variant prices or buying prices. The new-products template has one `price_taka` per product. The price importer (by SKU code) has no template download and no 'export current prices', so the owner has to assemble SKU codes by hand.
findings.evidence: PRODUCT_TEMPLATE = 'name,category,price_taka,sizes,colours,status,description' (variant-grid.ts:83-85). PriceImport renders a file input only, while product-import.tsx:64 offers a template link. PRICE_IMPORT_REQUIRED = ['sku','price_taka'] with optional barcode and note.
findings.proposal: (a) `GET /v1/catalog/prices/export?productId|categoryId` (read Catalog) → CSV sku,product,variant,price_taka[,compare_at_taka], to edit in Excel and re-import (round trip). (b) An optional `prices` column in the product template, e.g. `XL=2550|XXL=2650`, parsed in product-import.ts into `variantPrices` (D-422 already supports it server-side). (c) Buying prices by CSV belong to the supply module (sku, supplier_code, standard_cost_taka), behind read:cost; never in the catalog importer, which refuses cost columns by design (price-import.ts:17-22).

findings.what: A variant's barcode cannot be changed from the console. When a supplier ships with its own EAN on the tag, the brand cannot enter it, although `PUT /v1/catalog/skus/:id/barcode` exists and guards the internal range (D-603).
findings.evidence: grep finds no `setBarcode` or '/barcode' call in apps/console/src. The product grid shows the barcode with Copy and Print only (660-675).
findings.proposal: Add a pencil button on the barcode cell (update Catalog), or a 'Barcode' column in Edit mode. The scan field can fill it ('scan the supplier's tag'). Show the server's refusal for an internal-range or duplicate code. A null value restores the SKU code as the label payload, as the schema says (catalog.schemas.ts:216-224).

findings.what: Photos belong to the product only, not to a colour. The website cannot switch the gallery when a shopper picks Red, and a fashion product with 4 colours shows every colour's photos mixed together.
findings.evidence: product_images columns: product_id, file_id, position, alt_text, with no attribute value. The product detail response returns one `images` list for the product.
findings.proposal: Add a nullable `attribute_value_id` to catalog.product_images with a composite FK (org_id, attribute_value_id) → attribute_values (D-047), restricted to colour-kind values in the service. On the product page each photo gets a 'Colour: Any / Red / Blue' chip. The new-product photo picker gets the same chip per pending photo. The storefront product page returns `images` plus `colour` per image, so the website filters by the chosen colour.

findings.what: There is no 'Duplicate product'. A brand adding 50 products, many of them the same cut in another fabric, re-enters category, description, sizes, colours, per-variant prices, website fields and size chart each time.
findings.evidence: No duplicate or clone action in the catalog routes (grep). The new-product form starts from EMPTY state (new-product.tsx:103-117).
findings.proposal: Add a 'Duplicate' button on the product page that navigates to /catalog/new with `?from=<productId>`. The form pre-fills name ('… copy'), category, description, chosen axis values, per-variant prices (rowPrice keyed by the sorted value-id key), and website fields including size chart. It copies no stock and no costs; photos are optional and, if wanted, re-attached by fileId, since the unique index is per product (product_images_org_product_file_idx). Everything goes through the existing create path, so codes and barcodes stay server-made.

findings.what: Products and variants have no weight, so every courier booking is declared at the configured default (500 g for Pathao). Pathao prices by weight, so heavy items (jackets, sets) are under-declared and light ones over-charged.
findings.evidence: `weightGrams: null` on every booking (booking.service.ts:464). Pathao falls back to COURIER_PATHAO_DEFAULT_WEIGHT_GRAMS (pathao.adapter.ts:286), whose comment says 'this ERP does not track' weight (courier.config.ts:99).
findings.proposal: Add an optional `weight_grams integer` on catalog.products, with an optional per-SKU override, entered in the new-product form and Edit dialog. Booking sums qty × weight through CatalogApi (invariant 12) and falls back to the default when any line lacks one.

findings.what: In the Receive dialog, scanning an ARCHIVED variant's sticker adds a quantity for a row that is not shown. The hidden line is counted in the total and received into the archived SKU without the person seeing it.
findings.evidence: `<ScanIntoQuantities variants={variants} …/>` gets all variants (442), while QtyTable shows `variants.filter((variant) => variant.status === 'active')` (446). linesFrom() sends every non-empty entry (187-198). Supply and stock-in-hand accept archived SKUs (stock-in-hand.service.ts:903).
findings.proposal: Pass the same active-only list to ScanIntoQuantities and answer 'This variant is archived' on such a scan, or list archived variants in the table whenever they hold a quantity.

findings.what: Price fields accept 0 and negative amounts in the browser (takaToPoisha returns '0' or '-…'), so the long new-product form (photos chosen and all) is submitted and then refused by the server. In Edit prices one zero refuses the whole batch with a schema message.
findings.evidence: takaToPoisha's regex allows a leading '-' and zero (fields.tsx:166-176). `priceProblem` and aria-invalid test only `=== null` (new-product.tsx:196-199, 454). The server requires /^[1-9]\d*$/ (catalog.schemas.ts:34).
findings.proposal: Add a `positivePrice()` helper next to `positiveCost()` (variant-grid.ts:124-126), use it in the main price, row prices and edit-price inputs, and mark invalid cells with aria-invalid and a message, so the button stays disabled until fixed.

findings.what: The size chart is linked only inside the folded 'Website details' section, visible only to someone who may update Storefront. There is no category default, so all 50 panjabis need the same chart picked one by one.
findings.evidence: The WebDetails sizeChart Select sits inside `<details>` behind `mayWeb` (719-739). Category web fields are webVisible, featured, gender, description and imageFileId, with no size chart (catalog.service.ts:152-158).
findings.proposal: Add `default_size_chart_id` to category web fields. A product with no chart inherits its category's chart, shown as 'From category: Panjabi chart'. Show the chosen chart next to the Sizes chips in the new-product form, not only in the folded section.

findings.what: Two small labelling and visibility issues. The draft-pricing form's cancel button is labelled 'Remove line' (it closes the pricing form). The product page's Price range tile is hidden from roles without `read Stock`, even though price is catalog data.
findings.evidence: The pricing form's ghost button text is `st('supply.removeLine')` but it calls setPricing(null) (625-634). `<PermissionGate allowed={mayStock}>` wraps all four tiles, including PriceRange (254-264).
findings.proposal: Use a 'Cancel' key for the pricing form button. Move the Price tile outside the stock gate, or show it in the header next to the status badge.

items.feature: Delete a product, and a clear split between delete and archive
items.oldSite: Trash icon on every row of the product list, confirm, then a hard delete of the Mongo document plus CDN clean-up of images nothing else uses: elysium@HEAD app/(admin)/admin/products/AdminProductsClient.js:62-71 and 108-110; app/api/products/[id]/route.js:83-100 (deleteImageIfUnreferenced at 93-95). (The old admin is staged for deletion on branch erp-storefront of D:/Projects/elysium, so read it with `git show HEAD:<path>`.)
items.proposal:
ERP today: the product page has Archive and Reactivate only (apps/console/src/routes/catalog/product-detail.tsx:241-243, 380-397). Variants have per-row Archive (737-743, 759-774). There is no DELETE route (apps/server/src/modules/catalog/catalog.controller.ts:174-232). Archived products still show in the default list, because the status filter starts empty (products.tsx:166-171, 289-297). A hard delete is impossible today even for an untouched draft. The owner's 'can't do variant pricing' is likely about discoverability (the column placeholder shows the base price), the lack of bulk tools, and the missing per-variant cost outside opening stock.

Archive-not-delete is consistent with the invariants for products, variants and locations that have stock, orders or journals. It is missing for unused rows and for size/colour values and lists, which have no archive either.

Website size charts, hero and menu all have delete. Following the relayed owner instruction, I did not probe the M35b landing page builder at all; hero and menu are M33 website content, not that builder.

A delete that returns {id} therefore leaves no record of what was deleted. The existing deletes already lose data this way: a size chart's grid (storefront.service.ts:401-414), and menu children removed by the cascade (0103:142). The proposals' 'the audit interceptor records it' is not enough.

If an 'unused' SKU is purged while a till holds an unsynced sale of it, the cash sale can never be recorded. The 'no pos.sale_lines' eligibility check cannot see sales that have not synced yet.

COST_FIELDS (packages/contracts/src/permissions/subjects.ts:156-185) has no margin entry. cost-fields.test.ts:51 checks only database columns whose names match cost, wac, margin or profit, not computed response fields. If any route returns marginBps, a role without read:cost can derive cost from price and margin. The parity item puts the margin in packages/domain/src/money, served from an inventory route.
missing.whatToCheck: Either compute the margin only in the browser from the wacPoisha that cost roles already receive, or add marginBps and margin_bps (and lastUnitCostPoisha, standardUnitCostPoisha) to COST_FIELDS. Add a route-matrix cost sweep for the new routes.

missing.topic: A catalog CSV export with cost breaks invariant 5
missing.why: The parity item proposes GET /v1/catalog/export.csv with average cost and buying price for read:cost roles, and a buy_price_taka column in catalog CSV import and export. The catalog must never carry purchase cost (catalog/index.ts:26-41), and the price importer refuses cost columns by design (packages/domain/src/catalog/price-import.ts:17-22). serializeFor works on objects, not on CSV text.
missing.whatToCheck: Keep the cost export and import in supply or inventory routes. Put a selling-side-only export in catalog. Make sure CSV builders strip COST_FIELDS before serialising.

Nobody checked. Per-variant selling price IS in the deployed build: catalog-stock-ux is an ancestor of 93a9765 (D-422), so 'we can't do variant pricing' is about discoverability and missing cost, not a missing feature.

missing.topic: Rewriting promo scope lists conflicts with frozen terms
missing.why: The CRUD audit proposes rewriting promo.codes.category_ids, product_ids and sku_ids when a category or product is deleted. Discount terms are frozen by design (promo.controller.ts:87-90): only status changes, with an audit entry (promo.service.ts:632-656). Changing a code's scope after redemptions changes terms retroactively. Dangling ids in jsonb are harmless at runtime.
missing.whatToCheck: Decide: block the delete while any code names the id, or leave dangling ids and show 'deleted product' in the discount view. Do not mutate a redeemed code's terms. Changes go through PromoApi (invariant 12).

missing.why: CLAUDE.md requires integration tests against real Postgres for tenancy and permission changes, and the ledger-auditor for diffs touching tenancy or permissions. None of the delete proposals mention a cross-tenant test: a delete of org B's id from org A must return 404 and touch nothing. 'delete Catalog' is currently granted (matrix.ts:286) but used by no route, so it has never been exercised.
missing.whatToCheck: Plan route-matrix fixtures for every new DELETE and bulk route, an RLS cross-org delete test, and a check that roles without delete Catalog (warehouse, sales, marketing) get 403.

The CRUD audit also never notes that delete Catalog is unused today while image detach uses update Catalog (catalog.controller.ts:305-317).

contradictions: Product purge and legacy ids: the CRUD audit deletes storefront.legacy_ids rows in the purge transaction, while the parity item refuses the delete while a legacy_ids row exists. Under D-561 (docs/plans/M36.md:11-19) no products are imported, so product and variant legacy ids are empty and the clash is moot for products. It still matters for customers and for ncom variant addressing (storefront/index.ts:265-272).

Promo references in deletes: the CRUD audit blocks a category delete when ANY promo code names it and rewrites promo and campaign jsonb on a product purge. The parity item blocks only on an ACTIVE discount's category_ids (archived codes are left dangling) and blocks a product purge when it is in a discount's product_ids or a flash sale. Rewriting conflicts with the frozen discount terms (promo.controller.ts:87-90).
Archive marker for size and colour lists and values: the CRUD audit proposes an is_active column; the parity item proposes retired_at timestamptz. Pick one.

Last purchase cost read: the variant pricing review puts it in supply (GET /v1/supply/sku-costs, table supply.sku_purchase_prices), and the parity item in inventory (GET /v1/inventory/costs, table supply.sku_buy_prices). Different modules and different table names. An inventory route reading supply_lines would also break invariant 12.

Buying price by CSV: the variant pricing review says it belongs only in a supply importer, because the catalog importer refuses cost columns (price-import.ts:17-22). The parity item puts buy_price_taka in the catalog CSV export and import.

Discount restore: the CRUD audit says restore is api-only, because setStatus has no transition guard (promo.service.ts:632-656). The parity item says archive is one-way. Both are partly right: the server allows archived to active, the UI hides every action on archived rows (discounts.tsx:207).

LandingPage subject: the parity item proposes renaming it to Promotion. The CRUD audit and the relayed owner instruction say to leave the landing-page topic alone. Renaming touches that topic and the route matrix, so it is out of scope.

Campaign links: the parity item says 'Nothing exists yet' and lists them for this work. Branch m35b-web-marketing (commit 2749274) already builds campaign links console CRUD (storefront.custom_links), and they are M35b scope, not catalog scope.

Category order on the website: the parity item says the storefront orders categories alphabetically by slug. The website tree sorts siblings by position, then name (packages/domain/src/storefront/content.ts:108-135). Only the raw SQL orders by path. What is missing is a console control that sets position.

Re-adding an archived variant: the CRUD audit says the unique variant key refuses it. extendMatrix passes every existing key, archived ones included (skusOfProduct has no status filter, catalog.repository.ts:502-508), so matrixPlan reports it as unchanged: a silent no-op, not an error. The dialog already shows archived values as existing chips that cannot be unticked (product-detail.tsx:800-806, 844).

Activity log: the parity item says the interceptor already records every change with before and after. It records only the redacted request and response bodies (audit.interceptor.ts:178-201), the catalog writes no audit entries of its own, and there is no audit module api.ts to read through (only desk.repository.ts and preview/guard.ts read audit.audit_log).

Hands-on probe notes: 'merchandiser' is only the stack user's name; the account is org_admin. The parity item proposes a merchandiser role that does not exist, so the probe never tested a non-admin catalog editor.
